ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In attached Figure A, the left side is the rectangular wire frame abcd, the small metal circular ring L is located inside this rectangular wire frame and is in the same plane as the wire frame; at the ad side on the right side of the wire frame, a vertically placed solenoid is connected. Inside the solenoid a vertically upward arrow is drawn, marked as B, indicating that the positive direction of the externally applied magnetic field is upward along the solenoid axis. Attached Figure B is the graph of B changing with time t; in the stage from t1 to t2, B is in the positive-value direction and gradually increases, reaching the positive maximum value at t2. Reasoning: During the time t1～t2, the externally applied magnetic flux in the solenoid increases along the positive direction. According to Lenz's law, an induced current will be generated in the solenoid and its connected wire frame abcd, to hinder this increase of magnetic flux. This outer-frame current produces magnetic flux passing through the circular ring at circular ring L, and it increases with time; therefore an induced current will also be generated in circular ring L to hinder the increase of this through-ring magnetic flux, so the direction of the induced current in circular ring L is opposite to the current direction in the adjacent wire of the outer frame. Comparing each small segment of the circular ring with the adjacent wire segments of the rectangular outer frame: adjacent parallel currents are in opposite directions and repel each other; the repulsive forces received at the upper, lower, left, and right parts all point toward the interior of the circular ring. Therefore circular ring L has a tendency to contract.
